author: NorthEast News Desk
body: An Israeli airstrike killed a man, his wife and their two daughters, ages 8 and 12, in a house in Beit Lahiya in the northern Gaza Strip on Thursday, health officials told Reuters.

The Israeli military did not immediately comment on the reported strike. Residents and medics said at least six homes across Gaza had been hit during the previous two days, damaging nearby houses and tent shelters and prompting families to leave affected areas.

A U.S.-backed ceasefire reached in October 2025 ended large-scale fighting but did not stop all strikes or produce substantial progress toward a permanent settlement. Hamas and Israel have each accused the other of violating the agreement.

Gaza health officials say more than 1,300 Palestinians, most of them civilians, have been killed since the ceasefire took effect. The Israeli military says four Israeli soldiers have been killed over the same period. Those figures come from the respective parties and remain part of a developing conflict. Further information about Thursday’s strike is expected.
dek: Health officials said a man, his wife and their daughters, ages 8 and 12, were killed in a Beit Lahiya home as strikes intensified.
headline: Israeli strike kills family of four in northern Gaza, medics say
